verdict.rationale: LiveKit's own docs describe a step-by-step path to build voice agents in Python or Node.js, connect them to web, mobile, or phone sessions, and run AI models through LiveKit Inference, with turn detection and interruption handling. That makes it a first-party voice-agent integration path from live sessions. However, the evidence never explicitly describes the speech-to-text → model → text-to-speech pipeline stages. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the STT, LLM and TTS pipeline components and how they are wired, plus independent or hands-on corroboration of the voice-agent pipeline.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the vendor documents an integration path from a live session to a voice-agent pipeline of speech-to-text, a model, and text-to-speech

citations.quote: Build a simple voice agent with Python or Node.js in less than 10 minutes.
Build a voice agent in code with this step-by-step guide.
Bring your agent to life through a web or mobile app.
LiveKit Inference lets you run supported AI models directly within the LiveKit Cloud environment without requiring API keys.
Automatic turn detection and interruption handling
